ut_tooth_the.blurb: A distinctively shaped quartzite boulder in the lower part of the Ogden boulder field, set between Lobster Rock on one side and Hidden Rock on the other. Eleven problems cover a friendly-to-moderate spread: most sit around V1 and V2, with a handful of steeper lines stepping up through V3, V4 and V5 to a V6 at the top end. Expect a high top-out and sharp crimps on the south-facing side. The approach to the lower field is short, which makes the Tooth an easy stop on a session that links several nearby boulders, and the lower field can be climbed through much of the year.

ut_wall_of_colors.blurb: Wall of Colors is a roughly 45 m cliff in Logan Canyon, part of the same formation as the Wall of Jericho and a short stroll up-canyon from it. It holds about a dozen mostly sport lines, from 5.9 through the 5.12 range, with the bulk sitting around 5.10. Climbs here are long: several single pitches are big enough that a 70 m rope may not reach the ground, and a couple of routes go multi-pitch. The wall picks up morning sun and keeps it until mid-afternoon. A band of questionable rock halfway up and light traffic make a helmet a good idea.

ut_betagraph_the.blurb: The Betagraph is a quality sport crag in Logan Canyon with eleven routes, ten of them bolted and one traditional line. Grades run from the mid-5.7s up to 5.11, but the heart of the crag is 5.10, with a few harder 5.11 lines for the stronger climber. It sits on the river side of the canyon and takes about ten minutes of obvious trail to reach, a bit more of a walk than many Logan crags. The crag is a popular stop for climbers working through the canyon's 5.10 sport routes.

ut_bumble_bee_wall.blurb: Bumble Bee Wall is a steep, massive south-facing formation at Storm Mountain in Big Cottonwood Canyon. It is mostly traditional climbing with a few bolted sport lines, and some routes run to multiple pitches. Grades range from easy 5.6 up to 5.11, with the largest cluster around 5.9. The base is reached from the picnic area by a short trail down into a clearing, and some lines start from a ledge that needs a bit of fourth-class scrambling. Descents vary: some routes can be rappelled, some need a 60 m rope, and others finish by scrambling off.

ut_hyperform_wall.blurb: Hyperform Wall is the first wall climbers meet on arriving in Lone Peak Cirque, one of five areas in this alpine amphitheatre of the Central Wasatch. The climbing is all traditional and alpine in character, with several multi-pitch routes, including a four-pitch classic and a three-pitch line. Grades start at 5.8 and cluster in the 5.10s and low 5.11s, with a couple of lines a touch harder. Getting here means the cirque's long, steep approach, so plan for a full alpine day and bring a full trad rack.

ut_reef.blurb: The Reef is a limestone outcrop on the Grandeur Peak ridge above the Salt Lake valley, the lowest limestone band above the quartzite Quarry. It is a sport crag with eleven routes, mostly in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, a single 5.9, and one 5.13 at the top end. The wall faces north and stays cool, and it tends to be quiet. Expect a hike up a dirt road and then a switchback to reach it; be prepared for bolts that need checking and some routes set up as top-ropes.

ut_blob_s_your_uncle.blurb: Blob's Your Uncle is the cliff closest to the parking area in the Valley of Zion, in the Stansbury Mountains of Utah's West Desert, where the climbing is good-quality limestone. Eleven sport routes sit between 5.9 and 5.10, with six at 5.9 and five at 5.10, so it suits a warm-up or a moderate day. Most lines are single pitch, but a few multi-pitch routes, including a four-pitch outing, run all the way to the top of the colourful rock. The cliff is reached by walking along its base to the left of the gully.
